overall_summary: Exoplanet extremes and first-person 'What If You Fell Into...' survival/exploration hooks systematically outperform all other content, generating FACTVERSE's only 800-1,000+ view videos with top engagement rates (3.5%+ likes, active comments). Conversely, repeated cognitive psychology trivia ('Fake Memories', earworms) and low-stakes animal facts consistently flatline under 100 views with near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person Extreme Planetary Hazard ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (826 views, 15 likes) dominate the top tier.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor future space content in visceral, second-person physical consequence simulations with high sensory contrast rather than passive encyclopedic trivia.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Physical & Chemical Paradoxes in Space
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) sharply outperform standard astronomy facts.
winning_patterns.action: Focus strictly on alien worlds and cosmic phenomena featuring mind-bending visual states (extreme heat, atmospheric disintegration, metallic storms).

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 to 53 views, 0 likes) and 'Songs Stuck In Your Head' (17 to 71 views) repeatedly flopped.
weak_patterns.action: Halt generic psychology micro-facts entirely unless tied to a dark, high-stakes mystery or survival scenario.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' (11 views), 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views), and repeated 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' uploads (34-87 views).
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate static trivia statements; every short must open with kinetic tension, mystery, or bodily stakes.

next_video.concept: What would happen to the human body if you stepped onto KELT-9b, an ultra-hot Jupiter where vaporized iron tears apart molecules faster than a lightning strike.
next_video.opening_direction: First 2 seconds: High-contrast CGI view plunging directly toward a blisteringly bright blue-white gas giant, narrator: 'If you dropped onto KELT-9b, your suit wouldn't just melt—your atoms would literally be ripped apart.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's dayside is so hot (4,300°C) that even basic chemical bonds cannot exist, causing a glowing tail of boiling metal vapor stretching across space like a dying comet.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-converting 'What If You Fell Into...' first-person framework with extreme exoplanet thermodynamics, while introducing a totally unexploited exoplanet (KELT-9b).
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not repeat TrES-2b, Gliese 436b (Burning ice), 55 Cancri e (Diamond), WASP-76b (Molten iron), or HD 189733b (Glass rain).
Ensure the science of thermal molecular dissociation is accurate without generic sci-fi tropes.
